papers.title_zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲地区医护人员应对猴痘大流行的准备情况:快速回顾调查知识差距
papers.source_body_en: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.

papers.title: Synthesis and Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) of Hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamides against Orthopoxviruses.
papers.abstract: We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure-activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose-response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop potent antiviral compounds against orthopoxviruses, specifically monkeypox virus (MPXV), by improving the solubility and activity of previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the synthesis of 57 analogs of hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide, with the primary focus on evaluating their antiviral activity against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV).
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted antiviral structure-activity relationship (SAR)-directed synthesis and tested the compounds in primary VACV reporter assays and plaque assays against VACV and MPXV. They also assessed solubility improvements through amide N-methylation and evaluated ADME properties of compound 4f.
analysis.main_results: Many analogs showed nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency against VACV and MPXV without significant cytotoxicity. Compound 4f demonstrated >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM) and showed dose-response potency against MPXV in plaque assays.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that amide N-methylation significantly enhances solubility without compromising antiviral potency, offering a novel approach for lead development against orthopoxviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a promising lead compound (4f) for further development as an antiviral agent against monkeypox virus, potentially improving treatment options for mpox disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assays, and the evidence strength is moderate as the findings are based on laboratory experiments without clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the development of antiviral compounds against monkeypox virus (MPXV) by improving the solubility and activity of hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a. The researchers synthesized 57 analogs and evaluated their antiviral potency using in vitro assays against VACV and MPXV. Compound 4f showed significantly enhanced solubility while maintaining antiviral activity, with an EC50 of 0.69 μM. The study suggests that amide N-methylation is a viable strategy for lead development. However, the findings are based on laboratory experiments and lack clinical validation, limiting their evidence strength to moderate. The results have potential implications for the treatment of mpox disease, offering a new approach to antiviral development.

elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了 抗病毒药物 构效关系 (SAR) 指导的合成,并在初级 VACV 报告基因测定和针对 VACV 和 MPXV 的空斑测定中测试了这些化合物。他们还评估了通过酰胺 N-甲基化提高溶解度的情况,并评估了化合物 4f 的 ADME 特性。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了一种有前途的先导化合物 (4f),可用于进一步开发作为抗猴痘病毒的 抗病毒药物 药物,从而可能改善 治疗 针对 猴痘 疾病的选择。

papers.title_zh: 针对 正痘病毒 的羟基吡啶酮-3-甲酰胺的合成和构效关系 (SAR)。
papers.source_body_en: We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure-activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose-response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们之前已经鉴定出 Hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a 是对抗痘苗病毒 (VACV) 和猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 的有效 抗病毒药物,尽管其溶解度极低。在此,我们对总共 57 个类似物进行了 抗病毒药物 构效关系 (SAR) 指导和溶解度驱动的合成。在主要 VACV 报告基因测定中,许多类似物表现出纳摩尔至亚微摩尔 抗病毒药物 效力,而没有显着的细胞毒性,类似物 4m 显示出 10 倍的效力提高。针对 VACV 和 MPXV 的噬菌斑测定证实了 抗病毒药物 的强活性。我们还发现酰胺 N-甲基化通过破坏分子内氢键大大提高了溶解度。具体来说,我们确定了一种 N-甲基化类似物 (4f),其溶解度提高了 1000 倍以上,同时保留了效力 (EC50 = 0.69 μM)。此外,化合物 4f 在空斑测定中表现出针对 MPXV 的剂量反应效力以及非常有利的 ADME 特性。总的来说,我们目前的工作将 4f 描述为一种强大的 抗病毒药物 先导化合物,并巩固了酰胺 N-甲基化作为进一步先导化合物开发的可行方法。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了一种有前途的先导化合物 (4f),可用于进一步开发作为抗猴痘病毒的 抗病毒药物 药物,从而可能改善 治疗 针对 猴痘 疾病的选择。

papers.full_text: Nos últimos dois meses, a cidade do Rio de Janeiro registrou 74 casos de mpox, doença infecciosa causada pelo vírus monkeypox (MPXV). As lesões na pele são o sinal mais comum da doença. Elas também podem aparecer na boca, nos genitais ou na região anal. Outros sintomas incluem febre, ínguas, dor de cabeça, dores no corpo, calafrios e fraqueza. O número de casos na capital fluminense é sete vezes maior do que a quantidade apontada no mesmo período em 2025. No estado de São Paulo, 67 casos foram confirmados desde 4 de outubro, o que representa mais de um quinto de todos os casos da doença que o estado notificou neste ano. Os números nacionais não assustam: 832 casos e um óbito até 6 de novembro, contra cerca de 10,5 mil casos e 14 mortes em 2022. A média, porém, esconde o que realmente importa: a curva voltou a subir em setembro, com concentração em duas capitais e circulação de uma linhagem do vírus diferente daquela identificada no surto anterior. Atualmente, o clado Ib predomina entre as amostras analisadas. O surto de mpox de 2022 foi causado pelo clado IIb. Em virologia, um clado é um grupo de linhagens virais que compartilham um ancestral comum. Em resposta, o Ministério da Saúde comprou 25 mil doses da vacina contra a doença e orientou estados e municípios a aplicá-la por via intradérmica, técnica que pode multiplicar por cinco o número de pessoas vacinadas com o mesmo frasco. A vacina ganhou ainda mais importância no enfrentamento da mpox porque o único antiviral disponível para tratar a doença acaba de ser reprovado em dois ensaios clínicos. O que mudou no vírus O clado Ib, que predomina entre as amostras analisadas no Rio, foi identificado em 2023 no leste da República Democrática do Congo e levou a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) a declarar emergência internacional em agosto de 2024. Após uma queda sustentada nos casos notificados na África Central e Oriental, a OMS declarou o fim dessa emergência internacional. Foi quando a prevenção, a vigilância e o controle da doença passaram a integrar programas de saúde pública de longo prazo. No Instituto Nacional de Infectologia da Fiocruz (INI/Fiocruz), referência para a doença no Rio, 43 das 62 amostras identificadas entre setembro e outubro eram do clado Ib. Do total, somente 19 eram do clado IIb. A primeira detecção do clado Ib no Rio foi em março; o salto nos diagnósticos veio apenas em setembro. Em outubro, o INI atendeu 130 pessoas com suspeita da doença e confirmou 89 casos. O clado Ib chegou ao Brasil com viajantes. O INI/Fiocruz identificou os primeiros casos com evidência de transmissão comunitária (pessoas infectadas aqui, sem viagem recente) no início de 2026. A pergunta é se o clado Ib causaria quadros mais graves. Na África Central, ele foi associado a uma letalidade maior do que a observada com o clado IIb, mas essa diferença está também associada a fatores como desnutrição, coinfecções e falta de acesso a cuidados. No Rio, o INI/Fiocruz ainda não encontrou diferença clínica relevante entre os dois clados no grupo de pacientes acompanhado (a chamada coorte). O perfil das pessoas mais vulneráveis continua o mesmo: imunossuprimidos graves, gestantes e crianças pequenas. Cerca de 45% dos pacientes da coorte carioca vivem com HIV. Antiviral não passou no teste Durante o surto de 2022, o antiviral tecovirimat foi distribuído como tratamento para a mpox. O medicamento fora aprovado nos Estados Unidos para a varíola com base em estudos em animais, pois não havia como testá-lo em pessoas sendo a varíola uma doença erradicada do planeta desde 1980. A chegada da mpox - anteriormente conhecida como “varíola dos macacos”, que diante deste surto a OMS passou a recomendar ser chamada de “mpox” após relatos de uso racista e estigmatizante do nome anterior - ofereceu essa possibilidade. O ensaio PALM007 comparou o medicamento tecovirimat com placebo (sem princípio ativo) em 597 pacientes com o clado I na República Democrática do Congo. O tempo de resolução das lesões foi de sete dias no grupo que recebeu tecovirimat e de oito dias no grupo placebo. Essa não é uma diferença considerada relevante. Em fevereiro deste ano, o ensaio STOMP fechou questão sobre o clado II. O estudo acompanhou mais de 400 adultos distribuídos em dois grupos, um que recebeu o antiviral e outro que recebeu placebo. Até o 29o dia, as proporções estimadas de resolução das lesões foram semelhantes nos dois grupos (83% com tecovirimat e 84% com placebo). O estudo não encontrou evidência de que o tecovirimat fosse capaz de acelerar a resolução das lesões em adultos com mpox pelo clado II. Assim, a mpox continua a ser uma doença sem tratamento específico comprovado, o que desloca o peso da resposta para o diagnóstico precoce, o isolamento e a vacina. O medicamento continua reservado a pacientes com quadros graves e pacientes imunossuprimidos, mesmo sem evidência de que mude o curso da doença nesses pacientes. O que a vacina faz A única vacina para mpox é a MVA-BN (Jynneos), um imunizante contra a varíola de terceira geração, não replicante, produzido pelo laboratório Bavarian Nordic, na Dinamarca. Ela não foi testada em ensaios randomizados para avaliar sua eficácia contra mpox. O que existe são estudos observacionais (pesquisadores acompanham o que acontece na prática, sem determinar quem recebe a vacina) realizados no contexto do surto de 2022, todos com o clado IIb. Com base nesses estudos observacionais, a OMS estima que a vacina MVA-BN reduza o risco de mpox em 76% com uma dose e em 82% com duas, em comparação com pessoas não vacinadas. Os resultados variaram de um estudo para outro, sobretudo com uma dose. As estimativas de redução do risco foram de 35% a 86% com uma dose e de 66% a 90% com duas. Nos Estados Unidos, uma coorte de homens e mulheres trans em risco estimou uma proteção de 89% com o esquema completo e de 70% com uma única dose. Na Alemanha, a efetividade de uma dose foi de 58% no conjunto, mas de apenas 35% em pessoas vivendo com HIV, um dado relevante para o Brasil diante do fato de quase a metade dos casos brasileiros ocorrer nesse grupo. Em quem já foi exposto, a vacina reduz o risco de adoecer em cerca de 20% e parece atenuar a gravidade mesmo quando não impede a infecção. Pontos falhos Há dois pontos fracos nesses estudos. O primeiro diz respeito à duração da proteção: os níveis de anticorpos caem de forma acentuada entre 6 e 12 meses após a segunda dose, embora a resposta celular persista. Ainda não se sabe qual desses indicadores prediz melhor a proteção. O segundo diz respeito ao clado Ib. Não existe nenhum dado de efetividade clínica contra ele. O que há são estudos de laboratório: um grupo britânico mostrou em abril que o soro de 25 profissionais de saúde vacinados neutraliza o clado Ib, mas em níveis consistentemente menores que os observados contra o IIb. Proteção cruzada é provável, com base em modelos animais desafiados com clado I. O tamanho dessa proteção em pessoas, porém, é desconhecido. A via intradérmica, agora recomendada pelo Ministério da Saúde, foi adotada nos Estados Unidos e na Europa em 2022, com um quinto da dose, e produziu resposta imune comparável à da via subcutânea. O custo é operacional: exige treinamento e frascos que, descongelados, precisam ser usados em até quatro semanas. A decisão do ministério A compra das vacinas para o Brasil foi feita pelo Fundo Rotatório da Organização Pan-Americana da Saúde (OPAS). Com entrega prevista para daqui a três semanas, o pedido inicial de 20 mil doses aumentou para 25 mil após negociação com o fabricante. Antes disso, 3.650 doses do estoque nacional já tinham sido enviadas a nove unidades da Federação, incluindo Rio de Janeiro, Ceará e Distrito Federal. O SUS mantém a vacinação restrita a grupos definidos: pessoas vivendo com HIV, usuários de profilaxia pré-exposição (PrEP), profissionais de laboratório que manipulam o vírus e contatos de médio ou alto risco de casos confirmados. Não há vacinação em massa, o que está em linha com a orientação da OMS. A aplicação ocorre nos Centros de Referência de Imunização, não nas unidades básicas. A escolha tem lógica epidemiológica e uma limitação prática: a escassez mundial do imunizante. Mas o gargalo brasileiro nem sempre foi a oferta. Entre 2022 e 2023, o país distribuiu 49 mil doses da vacina para mpox e aplicou 14.395, menos de um terço. Em uma pesquisa com mais de 9.500 pessoas de diferentes orientações sexuais e identidades de gênero, apenas 4,9% relataram ter recebido ao menos uma dose. Os pesquisadores apontaram a oferta limitada e as barreiras de acesso como prováveis explicações para a baixa cobertura. É isso que decide se as 25 mil novas doses farão diferença. Para proteger quem está em risco antes da exposição, a vacina precisa chegar a essas pessoas a tempo de completar o esquema de duas doses. Para isso, precisa estar disponível nos serviços que oferecem profilaxia pré-exposição ao HIV (PrEP) e nos serviços de saúde sexual que esses pacientes já frequentam, não só em centros de referência que exigem cadastro e deslocamento. A prevenção é, neste momento, o único caminho para conter a doença. Quem apresentar lesões de pele novas, sobretudo com febre ou gânglios aumentados, deve procurar atendimento e evitar contato físico próximo até a avaliação. Pessoas com HIV devem manter o antirretroviral em dia. É a imunossupressão, mais que o clado, que define quem adoece gravemente com a mpox.

Os resultados variaram de um estudo para outro, sobretudo com uma dose. As estimativas de redução do risco foram de 35% a 86% com uma dose e de 66% a 90% com duas. Nos Estados Unidos, uma coorte de homens e mulheres trans em risco estimou uma proteção de 89% com o esquema completo e de 70% com uma única dose. Na Alemanha, a efetividade de uma dose foi de 58% no conjunto, mas de apenas 35% em pessoas vivendo com HIV, um dado relevante para o Brasil diante do fato de quase a metade dos casos brasileiros ocorrer nesse grupo. Em quem já foi exposto, a vacina reduz o risco de adoecer em cerca de 20% e parece atenuar a gravidade mesmo quando não impede a infecção. Pontos falhos Há dois pontos fracos nesses estudos. O primeiro diz respeito à duração da proteção: os níveis de anticorpos caem de forma acentuada entre 6 e 12 meses após a segunda dose, embora a resposta celular persista. Ainda não se sabe qual desses indicadores prediz melhor a proteção. O segundo diz respeito ao clado Ib. Não existe nenhum dado de efetividade clínica contra ele. O que há são estudos de laboratório: um grupo britânico mostrou em abril que o soro de 25 profissionais de saúde vacinados neutraliza o clado Ib, mas em níveis consistentemente menores que os observados contra o IIb. Proteção cruzada é provável, com base em modelos animais desafiados com clado I. O tamanho dessa proteção em pessoas, porém, é desconhecido. A via intradérmica, agora recomendada pelo Ministério da Saúde, foi adotada nos Estados Unidos e na Europa em 2022, com um quinto da dose, e produziu resposta imune comparável à da via subcutânea. O custo é operacional: exige treinamento e frascos que, descongelados, precisam ser usados em até quatro semanas. A decisão do ministério A compra das vacinas para o Brasil foi feita pelo Fundo Rotatório da Organização Pan-Americana da Saúde (OPAS). Com entrega prevista para daqui a três semanas, o pedido inicial de 20 mil doses aumentou para 25 mil após negociação com o fabricante. Antes disso, 3.650 doses do estoque nacional já tinham sido enviadas a nove unidades da Federação, incluindo Rio de Janeiro, Ceará e Distrito Federal. O SUS mantém a vacinação restrita a grupos definidos: pessoas vivendo com HIV, usuários de profilaxia pré-exposição (PrEP), profissionais de laboratório que manipulam o vírus e contatos de médio ou alto risco de casos confirmados. Não há vacinação em massa, o que está em linha com a orie…

As lesões na pele são o sinal mais comum da doença. Elas também podem aparecer na boca, nos genitais ou na região anal. analysis.research_question_and_background: A pesquisa busca entender a recorrência de casos de mpox no Brasil e a eficácia da vacina e dos tratamentos disponíveis, especialmente diante da circulação de uma nova linhagem do vírus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: O estudo analisa dados epidemiológicos de casos de mpox no Rio de Janeiro e em São Paulo, bem como informações sobre a vacina MVA-BN e os ensaios clínicos com o antiviral tecovirimat, incluindo comparações entre diferentes clados do vírus.
analysis.methods: Foram utilizados dados de notificação de casos, análise de amostras genéticas para identificar clados do vírus e estudos observacionais e clínicos para avaliar a eficácia da vacina e do antiviral tecovirimat.
analysis.main_results: No Rio de Janeiro, 74 casos de mpox foram registrados nos últimos dois meses, sendo 43 das 62 amostras coletadas entre setembro e outubro do clado Ib. O tecovirimat não mostrou eficácia significativa no tratamento de casos do clado II, e a vacina MVA-BN foi associada a uma redução estimada de 76% a 82% do risco de infecção com o clado IIb.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A recorrência de casos de mpox no Brasil está relacionada à circulação do clado Ib, que não foi efetivamente combatida pelos antivirais testados, reforçando a necessidade de estratégias de prevenção e controle baseadas na vacinação e na vigilância epidemiológica.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Os resultados destacam a importância da vacina MVA-BN no combate à mpox, especialmente em grupos vulneráveis como imunossuprimidos e pessoas com HIV, e reforçam a necessidade de monitoramento contínuo da circulação de novas linhagens do vírus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A eficácia da vacina foi baseada em estudos observacionais, e os ensaios clínicos com tecovirimat foram limitados a clados específicos, o que reduz a generalização dos resultados. A evidência é moderada.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the resurgence of mpox cases in Brazil, particularly in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, with a significant increase in the clade Ib of the MPXV. The research underscores the lack of proven efficacy of the antiviral tecovirimat against clade II mpox, as shown in the STOMP trial, and emphasizes the importance of the MVA-BN vaccine in prevention. Despite its role in reducing risk, the vaccine's effectiveness is based on observational studies, raising questions about its reliability. The findings stress the need for improved surveillance, early diagnosis, and targeted vaccination strategies, especially for vulnerable populations such as immunocompromised individuals and those living with HIV. The evidence is considered moderate due to the limitations of the studies used.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流行病涉及巴西 猴痘 的情况和疫苗功效以及治疗措施,特别是新病毒传播的情况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对里约热内卢和圣保罗的 猴痘 流行病学分析进行了研究,以了解有关疫苗 MVA-BN 和 抗病毒药物 特考韦瑞 临床的信息,包括不同分支之间的比较做病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 利用论坛通知、病毒鉴定、观察研究和疫苗功效临床分析以及 抗病毒药物 特考韦瑞 的遗传分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 里约热内卢的 74 个 猴痘 注册论坛中,有 43 个 62 个 amostras coletadas entre setembro 和 outubro do clado Ib。特考韦瑞 与 clado II 的情况相比,最有效,与 clado IIb 的感染风险相比,MVA-BN 疫苗可减少 76% 和 82% 的感染风险。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 巴西 猴痘 的情况报告与 Ib 循环有关,为了有效对抗抗病毒测试,需要制定预防和控制疫苗和警戒的策略流行病学。

papers.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
papers.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional genomic surveillance methods, which are slow and costly to compare at scale. The authors highlighted the need for a more efficient approach to handle the increasing volume of pathogen genomic data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduced MicroDUET, a dual-headed genomic foundation model, as a novel approach to pathogen surveillance. It evaluated the model's performance on held-out retrieval benchmarks and independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmarks.
analysis.methods: MicroDUET was developed by adapting a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads. One head was trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes to resolve evolutionary ancestry, while the other was trained to identify genes across taxa to assess phenotypic capability.
analysis.main_results: On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head achieved 80.3% accuracy for cellular queries and 66.6% for viral queries, while the function head reached 97.3% and 97.2% accuracy for gene family identification. MicroDUET demonstrated 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these results as evidence of MicroDUET's superior performance compared to existing genomic encoders. They noted that the model's ability to identify lineages and clades without prior training on these tasks represents a novel advancement in pathogen surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: MicroDUET has the potential to significantly improve the scalability and efficiency of genomic surveillance for mpox virus and other pathogens. It can aid in rapid identification of emerging lineages and resistance patterns, supporting timely public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, which may not capture the full scope of the model's performance. However, the results on held-out benchmarks suggest a high level of confidence in MicroDUET's capabilities for pathogen surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces MicroDUET, a dual-headed genomic foundation model designed to enhance pathogen surveillance. Traditional genomic surveillance methods are slow and costly, prompting the need for more efficient alternatives. MicroDUET adapts a ProkBERT backbone with two specialized heads to address both evolutionary ancestry and phenotypic capability. On held-out benchmarks, it achieved high accuracy in identifying species and gene families, outperforming 17 other genomic encoders. The model demonstrated the ability to detect mpox virus lineages and clades without prior training, and it can identify antimicrobial resistance patterns effectively. MicroDUET operates significantly faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments, making it a promising tool for scalable genomic surveillance. The study's abstract-only evidence provides a moderate confidence assessment, highlighting its potential for improving public health responses to emerging pathogens.

papers.title: Viro-BERT: Whole-Genome Attention for Robust Viral Pathogen Classification from Next-Generation Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and averages the window-level class probabilities in a Late Fusion Consensus layer. Because the windows are processed independently, memory use does not grow with genome length. We compared Viro-BERT with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, using the same segmentation and training protocol for all models. Viro-BERT reached 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. We then added random substitution noise to the test genomes. At 5% noise, the accuracy of the 1D-CNN fell by 5.57 percentage points, whereas Viro-BERT still classified 93.68% of genomes correctly. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT uses diagnostic signal from across the genome rather than from its 5' end alone. These results indicate that whole-genome context is needed for viral classifiers that remain reliable on noisy clinical data.

source_records.title: Viro-BERT: Whole-Genome Attention for Robust Viral Pathogen Classification from Next-Generation Sequencing Data.
source_records.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and averages the window-level class probabilities in a Late Fusion Consensus layer. Because the windows are processed independently, memory use does not grow with genome length. We compared Viro-BERT with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, using the same segmentation and training protocol for all models. Viro-BERT reached 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. We then added random substitution noise to the test genomes. At 5% noise, the accuracy of the 1D-CNN fell by 5.57 percentage points, whereas Viro-BERT still classified 93.68% of genomes correctly. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT uses diagnostic signal from across the genome rather than from its 5' end alone. These results indicate that whole-genome context is needed for viral classifiers that remain reliable on noisy clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces Viro-BERT, a novel deep learning model designed to classify viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing data. The research addresses the issue of Truncation Blindness, where traditional classifiers focus only on a fixed window at the start of the genome, neglecting the majority of the sequence. Viro-BERT processes overlapping windows across the entire genome, using a shared DistilBERT encoder and a Late Fusion Consensus layer to aggregate results. The model was compared with 1D-CNN, Bi-LSTM, and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, achieving 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. When tested with 5% random substitution noise, Viro-BERT maintained 93.68% accuracy, outperforming 1D-CNN, which dropped by 5.57 percentage points. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT utilizes diagnostic signals from across the genome rather than just the 5' end. These results highlight the importance of whole-genome context for reliable viral classification in noisy clinical data, with implications for improving diagnostic accuracy and genomic surveillance. The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the findings are based on a comparison with other models using the same segmentation and training protocol.

papers.title: Whole-genome characterization of Candidozyma auris isolates from a Korean tertiary care centre: clade II predominance, partly unexplained fluconazole resistance and a clade I isolate
papers.abstract: In South Korea, Candidozyma auris is dominated by ear-associated clade II isolates, but institution-based genomic data remain limited. We analysed 35 archived isolates from 29 patients at a tertiary care centre between 2017 and 2023 using antifungal susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing. Thirty-four isolates belonged to clade II, and one urine isolate recovered after inter-hospital transfer belonged to subclade Ib. Serial clade II isolates from the same patient clustered together and had lower pairwise SNP distances than different-patient pairs (median, 8.5 versus 181). Among the first isolates from 29 patients, 14 (48.3%) were fluconazole resistant. In first clade II isolates, recurrent curated coding variation was concentrated in TAC1B and ERG11 ; TAC1B F214S and W198C and ERG11 K143R occurred only in resistant isolates, but recognized coding variants did not account for all resistant isolates. Clade II isolates shared a broadly conserved subtelomeric deletion backbone, with variable chromosome 6 loss of selected glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor genes. The clade Ib isolate carried ERG11 Y132F, TAC1B A583S and a CDR1 V704L/E709D-like change and met CDC tentative breakpoints for resistance to fluconazole, amphotericin B and caspofungin. These findings refine the genomic profile of Korean clade II isolates and highlight the potential introduction of a distinct clade I lineage through healthcare transfer.

papers.title_original: Whole-genome characterization of Candidozyma auris isolates from a Korean tertiary care centre: clade II predominance, partly unexplained fluconazole resistance and a clade I isolate

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the genomic profile of Candidozyma auris isolates in South Korea and investigate the prevalence of fluconazole resistance, particularly in clade II isolates, to address the limited institution-based genomic data available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 35 archived isolates from 29 patients at a tertiary care centre between 2017 and 2023, including both clade II and a single clade Ib isolate recovered after inter-hospital transfer.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing and antifungal susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates, with a focus on identifying genomic variations and resistance patterns.
analysis.main_results: Thirty-four isolates belonged to clade II, while one urine isolate from a different patient belonged to subclade Ib. Serial clade II isolates from the same patient had lower pairwise SNP distances than those from different patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the predominance of clade II isolates in South Korea and suggest the potential introduction of a distinct clade I lineage through healthcare transfer, which may have implications for resistance mechanisms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the genomic diversity and resistance patterns of Candidozyma auris in South Korea, which can inform surveillance and infection control strategies in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on archived isolates, which may limit the ability to draw conclusions about recent trends or transmission dynamics, and the evidence is limited to genomic and susceptibility data.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes the genomic profile of Candidozyma auris isolates from a Korean tertiary care centre, revealing clade II predominance and the presence of a clade Ib isolate. It identifies genomic variations associated with fluconazole resistance in clade II isolates, highlighting the potential introduction of a distinct clade I lineage through healthcare transfer. The findings contribute to understanding the genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms of Candidozyma auris in South Korea, which may inform surveillance and infection control strategies. However, the study is limited to archived isolates, which may restrict its ability to capture recent transmission dynamics. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on genomic and susceptibility data without broader clinical or epidemiological context.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述韩国Candidozyma auris菌株的基因组特征,并探讨氟康唑耐药性的机制,特别是针对II类菌株,以应对目前基于机构的基因组数据有限的问题。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the genomic profile of Candidozyma auris isolates in South Korea and investigate the prevalence of fluconazole resistance, particularly in clade II isolates, to address the limited institution-based genomic data available.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 35 archived isolates from 29 patients at a tertiary care centre between 2017 and 2023, including both clade II and a single clade Ib isolate recovered after inter-hospital transfer.
analysis_en.methods: Whole-genome sequencing and antifungal susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates, with a focus on identifying genomic variations and resistance patterns.
analysis_en.main_results: Thirty-four isolates belonged to clade II, while one urine isolate from a different patient belonged to subclade Ib. Serial clade II isolates from the same patient had lower pairwise SNP distances than those from different patients.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the predominance of clade II isolates in South Korea and suggest the potential introduction of a distinct clade I lineage through healthcare transfer, which may have implications for resistance mechanisms.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the genomic diversity and resistance patterns of Candidozyma auris in South Korea, which can inform surveillance and infection control strategies in healthcare settings.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on archived isolates, which may limit the ability to draw conclusions about recent trends or transmission dynamics, and the evidence is limited to genomic and susceptibility data.

papers.title_zh: 韩国一家三级医疗机构中分离的Candidozyma auris菌株的全基因组特征:II类菌株占主导地位、部分无法解释的氟康唑耐药性以及I类菌株
papers.source_body_en: In South Korea, Candidozyma auris is dominated by ear-associated clade II isolates, but institution-based genomic data remain limited. We analysed 35 archived isolates from 29 patients at a tertiary care centre between 2017 and 2023 using antifungal susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing. Thirty-four isolates belonged to clade II, and one urine isolate recovered after inter-hospital transfer belonged to subclade Ib. Serial clade II isolates from the same patient clustered together and had lower pairwise SNP distances than different-patient pairs (median, 8.5 versus 181). Among the first isolates from 29 patients, 14 (48.3%) were fluconazole resistant. In first clade II isolates, recurrent curated coding variation was concentrated in TAC1B and ERG11 ; TAC1B F214S and W198C and ERG11 K143R occurred only in resistant isolates, but recognized coding variants did not account for all resistant isolates. Clade II isolates shared a broadly conserved subtelomeric deletion backbone, with variable chromosome 6 loss of selected glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor genes. The clade Ib isolate carried ERG11 Y132F, TAC1B A583S and a CDR1 V704L/E709D-like change and met CDC tentative breakpoints for resistance to fluconazole, amphotericin B and caspofungin. These findings refine the genomic profile of Korean clade II isolates and highlight the potential introduction of a distinct clade I lineage through healthcare transfer.
papers.abstract_zh: 在韩国,Candidozyma auris主要由与耳部相关的II类菌株组成,但基于机构的基因组数据仍较为有限。我们分析了2017年至2023年间在一家三级医疗机构中从29名患者分离的35株存档菌株,采用抗真菌药物敏感性试验和全基因组测序。其中34株属于II类菌株,而一株通过医院间转移获得的尿液分离株属于子类Ib。来自同一患者的连续II类菌株聚类在一起,其成对SNP距离低于不同患者之间的菌株(中位数,8.5 vs 181)。在29名患者的首次分离株中,有14株(48.3%)表现出氟康唑耐药性。在首次分离的II类菌株中,反复出现的编码变异主要集中在TAC1B和ERG11基因;TAC1B F214S和W198C以及ERG11 K143R仅出现在耐药菌株中,但已知的编码变异并未解释所有耐药菌株。II类菌株共享一个广泛保守的亚端粒区缺失骨架,但染色体6上某些糖基磷脂酰肌醇锚定基因的缺失情况存在差异。该Ib类菌株携带ERG11 Y132F、TAC1B A583S以及类似CDR1 V704L/E709D的变异,并符合CDC暂定的氟康唑、两性霉素B和卡泊芬净耐药性标准。这些发现细化了韩国II类菌株的基因组特征,并突出了通过医疗传播可能引入I类菌株的潜在可能性,这可能对理解耐药机制具有重要意义。

What to know There are two types of the virus that causes monkeypox, clade I and clade II. Both types can be spread, treated, and prevented in the same ways. Each clade has two subclades (clade Ia and clade Ib; clade IIa and IIb). Recent outbreaks of monkeypox have spread initially through intimate or sexual contact. In some cases, monkeypox was then spread within households. Recent travel-associated clade I monkeypox cases have almost exclusively been attributed to subclade Ib; there have been no deaths associated with these cases and most people had relatively mild illness. The ongoing global outbreak of clade IIb monkeypox that began in 2022 has caused more than 100,000 cases in more than 120 total countries. What to know Since January 2024, nearly 60,000 confirmed cases of clade I monkeypox have been reported globally, including more than 150 deaths. Newer outbreaks in several Western European countries are likely related to this ongoing outbreak. Transmission dynamics have changed. Only a small proportion of exported clade I monkeypox cases worldwide this year have originated in Central or Eastern African countries. Recent travel-associated clade I monkeypox cases have almost exclusively been attributed to subclade Ib; there have been no deaths associated with these cases and available data have detailed relatively mild disease courses. Outbreak overview In the United States The risk posed by the clade I monkeypox outbreak to most people within the United States remains low. The risk to men who have sex with men is low to moderate. Clade I cases in the United States have increased in frequency since March 2026. As of October 2026, there have been more than 190 clade I monkeypox cases reported in at least 30 states plus Puerto Rico. The majority of these cases are among gay, bisexual, or other men who have sex with men. Many of these cases: Had recently traveled from areas associated with the outbreak in Central and Eastern Africa; Reported sexual contact during travel to parts of Western Europe where newer outbreaks are being reported; OR Reported sexual contact with people who had traveled from these areas. Since August 2026, an increasing proportion of clade I cases in the United States have been reported in individuals with no recent international travel or known links to people who had recently traveled. Cases with presumed domestic transmission have been reported in at least 16 jurisdictions, indicating a likely transition to sustained clade Ib transmission in the United States. CDC expects to see additional cases of both travel-related and domestically acquired cases of clade Ib occurring across the United States. Preventing Monkeypox While Traveling Learn where monkeypox is spreading and how to lower your risk of getting it during travel. In Central and Eastern Africa Clade Ia monkeypox outbreaks began impacting western areas of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in 2024. Available data indicate that clade Ia monkeypox has spread through sexual contact, regular household contact, and encounters with infected dead or live wild animals. Clade Ib monkeypox cases initially impacted eastern areas of DRC in late 2023. This subclade has driven much of the spread throughout Central and Eastern Africa and most travel-associated cases to other parts of the world. Available data indicate that these cases at first spread through heterosexual intimate or sexual contact between adults, then spread likely occurred within households, including to children. The disease spread in 2024 and 2025 to neighboring countries of DRC, only some of which are endemic for the virus that causes monkeypox, and sustained local spread occurred. Outside Central and Eastern Africa Several countries in other parts of Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America, as well as Australia, have confirmed clade I monkeypox cases mostly in travelers who'd recently been in areas with clade I outbreaks. To date, there have been more than 300 clade Ib cases in high-income countries, and no deaths have been reported. Several countries in Western Europe are reporting clade Ib monkeypox cases among individuals who had no documented history of international travel. These cases were likely related to intimate or sexual exposure among men who have sex with men. We expect additional cases in Europe and the United States. For data since January 1, 2024, see 2022-24 Monkeypox (Monkeypox) Outbreak: Global Trends (shinyapps.io). Confirmed cases include those that are laboratory confirmed as monkeypox virus and may include cases only confirmed as orthopoxvirus. These data are provided for situational awareness and are subject to change. Clade I monkeypox and children Early in the Central and Eastern African outbreak that began in 2024, a high proportion of suspected cases in some areas were reported in children younger than 15 years of age. Historically, cases of monkeypox in children where monkeypox occurs regularly often happen after contact with wild animals that carry the disease. People then can spread the disease to close contacts, including in their households. The number of children with suspected monkeypox in this outbreak is probably due to spread within and between close households, the large number of younger people in affected countries, misdiagnosis of other diseases (such as measles), poor sanitary conditions, limited access to health services, and a high level of food insecurity and malnutrition. Based on what we know today, we don't expect to see the same sort of pattern in the United States for several reasons, including smaller household sizes, access to cleaning and disinfecting products, and improved access to medical care, equipment, and information about preventing spread while caring for patients. Notably, there are no consistent reports of schools as drivers of monkeypox transmission during any recent outbreaks. If cases of clade I monkeypox do happen in children the United States, CDC has clinical and public health guidance for reporting, testing, and effective case management. What CDC is doing CDC has been supporting DRC monkeypox research and response for more than 20 years. CDC and other U.S. government agencies have continued working in-country with partners in affected areas on disease surveillance, building local laboratory capacity, strengthening public health and laboratory workforce capacity, case investigation, case management, infection prevention and control, border health, and risk communication and community engagement. In the United States, CDC monitors both clade II and clade I monkeypox cases across the United States and follows surveillance reports to monitor for any changes in demographics, disease severity, or case counts by jurisdiction. CDC also performs surveillance testing to identify monkeypox clade for specimens sent to CDC's poxvirus laboratory. CDC staff brought laboratory supplies and trained local staff on laboratory equipment Resources Global Monkeypox: Current Situation There are outbreaks of clade I and clade II monkeypox around the world. analysis.time: Since January 2024, the outbreak has been ongoing. As of October 2026, the situation is being monitored, with an increasing proportion of cases reported since August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak has been reported globally, with a focus on the United States, where cases have been documented in at least 30 states plus Puerto Rico. The majority of cases in the U.S. are among gay, bisexual, or other men who have sex with men.
analysis.event: Clade I monkeypox outbreaks have been reported globally, including in the United States. The CDC has confirmed these outbreaks and is monitoring their spread, particularly among men who have sex with men and through domestic transmission.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of October 2026, more than 190 clade I monkeypox cases have been reported in the U.S. Globally, nearly 60,000 confirmed cases of clade I monkeypox have been reported, with over 150 deaths. The risk to most people in the U.S. remains low, but the risk to men who have sex with men is low to moderate. No deaths have been reported in clade Ib cases in high-income countries.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC is actively monitoring the outbreak, providing guidance for prevention, testing, and case management. The situation is ongoing, with expectations of additional cases in Europe and the U.S. The data are subject to change and provided for situational awareness.

analysis.brief_en: The CDC has reported ongoing clade I monkeypox outbreaks globally since January 2024, with nearly 60,000 confirmed cases and over 150 deaths. In the United States, more than 190 cases have been reported in at least 30 states and Puerto Rico as of October 2026, with the majority among men who have sex with men. The risk to most people in the U.S. remains low, but it is moderate for men who have sex with men. Transmission dynamics have changed, with an increasing proportion of cases in the U.S. involving domestic spread rather than international travel. The CDC is actively monitoring the outbreak and expects more cases in Europe and the U.S. They are providing guidance for prevention, testing, and case management, emphasizing that the data are subject to change and for situational awareness. No deaths have been reported in clade Ib cases in high-income countries, and these cases are associated with relatively mild disease courses.

The risk to most people in the U.S. remains low, but it is moderate for men who have sex with men. Transmission dynamics have changed, with an increasing proportion of cases in the U.S. involving domestic spread rather than international travel. The CDC is actively monitoring the outbreak and expects more cases in Europe and the U.S. They are providing guidance for prevention, testing, and case management, emphasizing that the data are subject to change and for situational awareness. No deaths have been reported in clade Ib cases in high-income countries, and these cases are associated with relatively mild disease courses.

analysis_en.time: Since January 2024, the outbreak has been ongoing. As of October 2026, the situation is being monitored, with an increasing proportion of cases reported since August 2026.
analysis_en.location_and_population: The outbreak has been reported globally, with a focus on the United States, where cases have been documented in at least 30 states plus Puerto Rico. The majority of cases in the U.S. are among gay, bisexual, or other men who have sex with men.
analysis_en.event: Clade I monkeypox outbreaks have been reported globally, including in the United States. The CDC has confirmed these outbreaks and is monitoring their spread, particularly among men who have sex with men and through domestic transmission.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: As of October 2026, more than 190 clade I monkeypox cases have been reported in the U.S. Globally, nearly 60,000 confirmed cases of clade I monkeypox have been reported, with over 150 deaths. The risk to most people in the U.S. remains low, but the risk to men who have sex with men is low to moderate. No deaths have been reported in clade Ib cases in high-income countries.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC is actively monitoring the outbreak, providing guidance for prevention, testing, and case management. news.source_body_en: The CDC has reported ongoing clade I monkeypox outbreaks globally since January 2024, with nearly 60,000 confirmed cases and over 150 deaths. In the United States, more than 190 cases have been reported in at least 30 states and Puerto Rico as of October 2026, with the majority among men who have sex with men. The risk to most people in the U.S. remains low, but it is moderate for men who have sex with men. Transmission dynamics have changed, with an increasing proportion of cases in the U.S. involving domestic spread rather than international travel. The CDC is actively monitoring the outbreak and expects more cases in Europe and the U.S. They are providing guidance for prevention, testing, and case management, emphasizing that the data are subject to change and for situational awareness. No deaths have been reported in clade Ib cases in high-income countries, and these cases are associated with relatively mild disease courses.

news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Africa has issued a situation update on the mpox outbreak in Uganda, dated 11 December 2024. Mpox cases rise, prompting expanded county public health outreach San Diego County says 16 cases of mpox have been confirmed since October, bringing total to 48 so far this year Share this: Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email Share on Reddit (Opens in new window) Reddit Minseung Chu, clinical assistant professor at UIC College of Nursing, prepares mpox vaccines at a vaccine event at Calor, a Latino nonprofit catering to people with HIV, in the Humboldt Park neighborhood of Chicago on Oct. 30, 2024. (Tess Crowley/Chicago Tribune) By City News Service | news@socalnews.com PUBLISHED: November 13, 2026 at 3:38 PM PST | UPDATED: November 15, 2026 at 5:12 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... San Diego County on Friday reported an increase in local mpox cases with 16 confirmed since October, and 48 total so far this year, an increase from 35 reported in 2025.An infectious disease transmitted through close contact, including sexual contact, mpox has two variants that cause disease in people, Clade I and Clade II. According to the county, Clade II has driven most cases since the virus first appeared in the region in 2022. Clade I has circulated in California since 2025, and San Diego County health officials have confirmed 10 Clade I cases since July 2026.The symptoms of both variants are similar and the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine protects against both types, a county statement read. Of the 16 cases reported since October, 10 occurred in unvaccinated people.California’s Department of Public Health first reported an increase in Clade I infections across the state in October 2025, tying it to returning travelers from Europe where Clade I cases were occurring.The more recent rise is believed to stem from those traveling within the state. As a result, San Diego County has increased its public reporting of cases from monthly to weekly.“With this recent increase in local cases, we are reminding people at risk to get the two-dose vaccine as soon as possible,” said Dr. Ankita Kadakia, county deputy public health officer. “It remains the best way to protect yourself and those around you. If you still need the second dose, it is never too late to receive it.”The disease has been spread in the San Diego region since 2022 when infections peaked at 469 cases. In years since, new cases have remained below 100 annually, the county reports.Symptoms include a rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, body aches and fatigue. The rash or sores may be located anywhere on the body. This includes hands, feet, chest, face, mouth and genitals.“Although most cases are mild, the vaccine is very effective at preventing severe illness, hospitalization and death,” the county statement read.Anyone who may be at increased risk for mpox, or who believes they may have been exposed, should contact their healthcare provider and discuss vaccination options. San Diego County has JYNNEOS vaccines available at its Sexual Health Clinics located in regional Public Health Centers. Published in BMC Infectious Diseases, the study evaluated three mother–infant pairs treated across three hospitals between January and May 2025. In each documented instance, maternal illness went undetected until neonates developed symptomatic illness requiring medical attention, underscoring ongoing diagnostic hurdles at the maternal–neonatal interface in endemic regions. The study sought to address significant gaps in the characterization of mpox during pregnancy and the immediate neonatal period. Retrospective review of clinical records allowed investigators to examine maternal clinical histories, potential transmission pathways, clinical presentations, and ultimate patient outcomes. Cases were identified during routine hospital care when infants presented with characteristic vesiculopustular illness. The clinical cohort comprised three male neonates whose diagnoses were laboratory-confirmed using real-time polymerase chain reaction testing performed on lesion swabs. Discover more infectious diseases infection Infections infections Check Symptoms Clinical histories revealed that two of the mothers developed fever and vesiculopustular eruptions during their third trimester of pregnancy. The third mother experienced a brief febrile episode without an apparent or documented rash approximately one day prior to delivery. None of the mothers were clinically suspected of having mpox before giving birth, and none underwent diagnostic molecular testing for monkeypox virus infection during their pregnancies or deliveries. All three male infants subsequently exhibited fever and widespread vesiculopustular skin lesions emerging between days 4 and 9 of life, eventually presenting to clinical facilities between days 14 and 16. While clinicians considered administering the antiviral agent tecovirimat, the drug was unavailable for clinical use within Nigeria during the active study period. Clinical trajectories diverged among the three hospitalized neonates. Two infants achieved full recovery following supportive inpatient therapy. Conversely, the third neonate died at home on day 24 of life after an interruption of hospital care. Because no post-mortem examination was performed, the precise immediate cause of death could not be verified by medical teams. Discover more Study Biology Read Med Journals Shop Baby Gear Track Pregnancy Buy Maps The documented presentations demonstrate the substantial clinical and operational challenges surrounding mpox management at the maternal–newborn interface across endemic settings. When maternal infections go unconfirmed, clinical investigation depends almost entirely on the emergence of early, visible manifestations in newborns. Sustaining continuous inpatient management represents another critical priority identified by the investigators. The authors conclude that improving frontline diagnostic suspicion, expanding access to timely molecular testing, and ensuring unbroken continuity of care will be vital to mitigating risks for infected mothers and neonates. analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 13, 2026, in BMC Infectious Diseases highlights the challenges of diagnosing maternal mpox infections in southern Nigeria. The research, conducted between January and May 2025, examined three mother–infant pairs treated in three hospitals. The study underscores the need for improved diagnostic suspicion and access to molecular testing, as well as continuous inpatient care, to address risks associated with mpox during pregnancy and the neonatal period. The antiviral tecovirimat was unavailable for use in Nigeria during the study period, limiting treatment options.

news.content: Health & Fitness Mpox Cases On The Rise In San Diego County, Health Officials Warn Officials say evidence of local transmission has prompted increased monitoring and renewed vaccination efforts. SAN DIEGO, CA — San Diego County health officials are expanding outreach efforts amid a rise in mpox infections, with 16 cases confirmed since October and 48 reported so far this year. The county reported 35 cases in all of 2025. Mpox spreads through close physical contact, including sexual contact. Two types of the virus, Clade I and Clade II, cause illness in humans. Clade II has accounted for most local cases since mpox emerged in the region in 2022. Find out what's happening in San Diegofor free with the latest updates from Patch. Clade I has circulated in California since 2025. San Diego County health officials have confirme 10 cases of Clade I mpox since July, with evidence suggesting the virus is spreading locally. Of the 16 cases reported since October, 10 involved people who were not vaccinated, according to health officials. Find out what's happening in San Diegofor free with the latest updates from Patch. "With this recent increase in local cases, we are reminding people at risk to get the two-dose vaccine as soon as possible," said Dr. Ankita Kadakia, the county's deputy public health officer. "It remains the best way to protect yourself and those around you. If you still need the second dose, it is never too late to receive it." Symptoms include a rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, body aches and fatigue. The rash or sores can appear anywhere on the body, including hands, feet, chest, face, mouth and genitals. Although most infections are mild, the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine protects against both types of mpox and helps prevent severe illness, hospitalization and death, officials said. Mpox cases in San Diego County peaked at 469 in 2022 and have remained below 100 annually since then. In response to the recent increase, the county has begun reporting mpox cases weekly instead of monthly. Health officials encourage people at increased risk or those who may have been exposed to contact their health care provider about vaccination. Vaccines are available through county sexual health clinics, including for uninsured and underinsured residents. For more information, visit the county's mpox webpage. Residents can also sign up for updates by texting COSD MPOX to 98256. Get more local news delivered straight to your inbox. Sign up for free Patch newsletters and alerts

news.content: Monday, 16 November 2026dailybeirut.com AR|EN|FR|ES|RU News Lebanon World Business Sports Football Technology and ScienceArtificial Intelligence Magazine Culture and Society Lifestyle Miscellaneous Health Home/Health Health Brazil records first mpox death of 2026 amid rising cases Brazil confirmed its first mpox fatality in 2026, with authorities monitoring a rise in infections that remains below historical peak levels. ·November 15, 2026 at 8:22 AM·1 min read Share Contents Case data and fatality details Government response measures Nature of the virus Global context and regional spread Brazil has recorded its first death from mpox in 2026. While case numbers have increased, Brazilian health authorities do not classify the current situation as an outbreak, according to a public health institute. Case data and fatality details The Fiocruz Institute, which operates under Brazil’s Ministry of Health, reported 1,009 confirmed viral infections this year. The fatal case occurred in Rio de Janeiro, where confirmed infections between September and November doubled compared to the rest of the year. Government response measures In response to the trend, the government strengthened surveillance protocols and purchased 25,000 additional doses of the mpox vaccine. Despite these actions, officials maintain that infection rates remain significantly lower than the historic peak observed in 2022. Nature of the virus Mpox is caused by a virus belonging to the poxvirus family. Symptoms include fever, muscle pain, and large skin lesions resembling boils, with potential for fatal outcomes. Transmission occurs from animals to humans or between people through close physical contact. Global context and regional spread The World Health Organization declared mpox a public health emergency of international concern in both 2022 and 2024 due to rapid spread in certain countries. Most Brazilian cases this year were concentrated in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, two of the nation’s three most populous states within a total population of 214 million. NIAID / CC BY 2.0 By City News Service Published November 13, 2026 11:34 PM SAN DIEGO, Calif. (KESQ) - San Diego County today reported an increase in local mpox cases with 16 confirmed since October 2026, and 48 total so far this year, an increase from 35 reported in 2025. An infectious disease transmitted through close contact, including sexual contact, mpox has two variants that cause disease in people, Clade I and Clade II. According to the county, Clade II has driven most cases since the virus first appeared in the region in 2022. Clade I has circulated in California since 2025, and San Diego County health officials have confirmed 10 Clade I cases since July 2026. The symptoms of both variants are similar and the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine protects against both types, a county statement read. Of the 16 cases reported since October 2026, 10 occurred in unvaccinated people. California's Department of Public Health first reported an increase in Clade I infections across the state in October 2025, tying it to returning travelers from Europe where Clade I cases were occurring. The more recent rise is believed to stem from those traveling within the state. As a result, San Diego County has increased its public reporting of cases from monthly to weekly. "With this recent increase in local cases, we are reminding people at risk to get the two-dose vaccine as soon as possible,'' said Dr. Ankita Kadakia, county deputy public health officer. "It remains the best way to protect yourself and those around you. If you still need the second dose, it is never too late to receive it." The disease has been spread in the San Diego region since 2022 when infections peaked at 469 cases. In years since, new cases have remained below 100 annually, the county reports. Cases in Riverside County remain low, with 16 reported all year. Symptoms include a rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, body aches and fatigue. The rash or sores may be located anywhere on the body. This includes hands, feet, chest, face, mouth and genitals. "Although most cases are mild, the vaccine is very effective at preventing severe illness, hospitalization and death,'' the county statement read. Anyone who may be at increased risk for mpox, or who believes they may have been exposed, should contact their healthcare provider and discuss vaccination options. San Diego County has JYNNEOS vaccines available at its Sexual Health Clinics located in regional Public Health Centers. Log In Register Search: Search: News All Arts Crime Politics Perspectives Things to Do Local Events Post an Event Business Events Games Jobs Contact Us Digital Editions Webinars Podcasts Health New York City sees increase in mpox cases By Matt Tracy ... Comments Posted on November 13, 2026 The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene’s offices in Long Island City, Queens. Matt Tracy After a mostly quiet summer, mpox cases started to increase in New York City in August and there have been dozens of cases per month since then, according to the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. The latest numbers show the lingering impact of mpox, which has overwhelmingly impacted men who have sex with men since a 2022 outbreak hit the US. The city saw as many as 100 cases per day at one point that year as activists pushed the Biden administration for more doses of the Jynneos vaccine, which protects against mpox. Following the initial outbreak, mpox cases dipped, but they nonetheless continued to circulate in New York City, where cases have gone up and down over the course of several years. Early last year, the city was seeing very few cases — sometimes none or only one or two in a given week — but cases started increasing in April of 2025 and gradually rose until hitting 23 in one week in early October of last year. From there, cases decreased over the course of several months, and there were only a handful of cases from the spring of 2026 until the late summer. However, cases started to creep up in the latter part of this summer: The week of Aug. 29 saw six cases — the most since March — and subsequent weeks continued to see more cases, eventually hitting 13 in one week in the middle of September. There were 41 cases reported across the five boroughs between Sept. 6 and Oct. 3. After reaching a weekly high of 19 cases on Sept. 19, the city has still seen elevated cases: Since then, five out of seven weeks have had at least eight cases — more than the city ever saw in a week from late March until September. City health officials are attributing the uptick to “seasonal increases” and insisted that cases are now declining, even as cases have increased in consecutive weeks. “Mpox cases follow a seasonal pattern that typically decrease after summer, with a late-summer peak this year,” the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene told Gay City News in a written statement. “Data recently posted to the Health Department website shows cases are now trending downward. While we are not noticing a unique increase in cases compared to the previous year, we have seen recent cases of clade I mpox including among people returning from travel.” Meanwhile, there has also been a slight increase in mpox cases in other parts of New York State. According to the New York State Department of Health’s mpox data, which shows cases outside of New York City, the rest of the Empire State saw either no cases or one case per month from March until August, but there were six cases in September and 19 cases in October. According to health officials, the variant of mpox that has circulated in New York and the US is Clade II. A different kind of mpox, clade I, has been associated with outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and other countries in Central and Eastern Africa. In March of this year, New York City reported its first case of Clade I. “New Yorkers at risk for mpox, including those who may be traveling to Europe, should still get vaccinated,” the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene said. “The NYC Health Department recommends starting and completing the two-dose JYNNEOS series. If you’ve already received the first dose, it is never too late to get the second. To find a location near you, please visit nyc.gov/healthmap or a Health Department Sexual Health Clinic for low-to-no cost vaccination.” Conversations Profile All comments are subject to our Community Guidelines.
